source_read: Saved PubMed Central page text (PMC5419581, author manuscript), read in full: abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, figure legends, disclosures, funding and author contributions; reference list checked for the cited studies. The forest plots (Figures 1–3) and the Figure 4 schematic are images and are not in the saved text; the supplement was not available.

anchors.note: Anchor text revised twice after the round-1 snapshot, the second time today while this check was running (it is now marked as checked at the stated place); verdict given on the text as it stands at 03:25. Confirmed in the source: one g, 1.16 (0.56 to 1.76), for the two early-abstinence studies (refs 51–52; mean abstinence 2.6 and 19 days) with no pooling method; 1.68 (0.86 to 2.5) for Johanson et al. (2006, ref 28), described as three months of abstinence; three VMAT2 values printed for four studies, all positive, while the DAT, D2/3 and release reductions are negative. The editors’ calculation reproduces from the Boileau et al. (2016) values on the encyclopedia’s card (3.09, SD 0.71, n=28 vs 2.41, SD 0.34, n=22): g 1.16 (0.56 to 1.76). Kish et al. (2017) describe the Johanson study as about three years of abstinence (VMAT2 section), confirmed; Hart et al. (2012) is not among this checker’s sources. Wording only: the anchor calls 1.16 ‘pooled’ while also saying the review does not state how it was combined; ‘the combined 1.16’ would be consistent.

108 people vs 126 controls, p<0.001. The nine studies are refs 27–35, including one of people using dexamphetamine recreationally (Schouw et al., 2013) and two DAT studies from Volkow's group (2001, J Neurosci; 2015, NeuroImage); now noted on key finding 0 of the card.
